brief.scope: Security audit of PR 101 at this head: the receipt lever ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py, the four modules under ops/devlane/harness/receipt/ (extracted verbatim from the previous repository under an owner grant; a finding against them is a finding, not a fix), the contract ops/devlane/harness/evidence.cue, and the tests ops/devlane/harness/tests/test_receipt.py by another harness. Read in/extraction-checklist-receipts-20260911.md and in/brief-receipt-tests-20260911.md WHOLE; the checklist's nineteen items and the contract are the only requirements; the two flagged decisions (checklist items 6 and 12) are the owner's to rule, not defects. Hunt: argv or cwd escaping the repository root, receipts written outside .dev/records/receipts, a digest that does not bind the fields it names, a refusal off the wire. Each finding quotes the checklist item or contract field it violates or is marked observation.

findings.claim: Checklist item 10 requires cwd to be "relative to the repository root, never absolute." verify validates only field names, then executes at unchecked body["cwd"]. A twelve-key receipt with cwd "/" ran outside the snapshot and was reported verified.
findings.reproduce:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - <<'PY'
import hashlib,json,os,subprocess
from pathlib import Path
head=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()
body={'kind':'receipt','claim':'probe','argv':['/bin/pwd'],'cwd':'/','head_sha':hashlib.sha256(head.encode()).hexdigest(),'tree_dirty':False,'exit_code':0,'duration_ms':0,'stdout_sha256':hashlib.sha256(b'/\n').hexdigest(),'stderr_sha256':hashlib.sha256(b'').hexdigest(),'actor':'Audit <a@b>','at':'2026-09-11T00:00:00Z'}
fd=os.memfd_create('receipt'); os.write(fd,json.dumps(body).encode()); os.lseek(fd,0,0)
p=subprocess.run(['python3','ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py','verify',f'/proc/self/fd/{fd}'],pass_fds=(fd,),capture_output=True,text=True)
print(p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr); assert p.returncode==0 and 'verified' in p.stdout
PY

findings.claim: Checklist item 11 requires receipts to live under .dev/records/receipts. The entire path is excluded from dirty detection and write_receipt follows a directory symlink without resolving or checking containment, allowing a receipt to be written outside the repository while stdout reports an internal path.
findings.reproduce: bash -eu -c 'r=$PWD; d=$(mktemp -d); git init -q "$d/repo"; mkdir -p "$d/repo/.dev/records" "$d/out"; printf x > "$d/repo/a"; printf base > "$d/repo/.dev/records/base"; git -C "$d/repo" add .; git -C "$d/repo" -c user.name=a -c user.email=a@b commit -qm one; ln -s "$d/out" "$d/repo/.dev/records/receipts"; (cd "$d/repo" && WF_AGENT="Audit <a@b>" python3 "$r/ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py" record --claim probe -- true); find "$d/out" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "*.json" -print -quit | grep .'

findings.claim: Checklist item 11 says the filename digest makes a receipt tamper-evident, but load_receipt never recomputes the canonical digest. Modified fields are accepted under the original digest reference.
findings.reproduce:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util,json
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('lever',Path('ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py').resolve()); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
original='704eafbc6d925095cdaed78431740df4ee4ce791b7696bee976345bed9ebee44'
body=json.loads((Path('.dev/records/receipts')/(original+'.json')).read_text()); body['claim']='tampered but accepted'; raw=m.canonical.dumps(body)
target=Path.cwd()/'.dev/records/receipts'/(original+'.json'); real=Path.is_file
def exists(p): return p==target or real(p)
def read(p,**k): return raw if p==target else (_ for _ in ()).throw(AssertionError(p))
with patch.object(Path,'is_file',exists),patch.object(Path,'read_text',read): loaded,_=m.load_receipt(Path.cwd(),original)
actual=m.canonical.digest(loaded); print(original,actual,loaded['claim']); assert actual!=original
PY

findings.claim: The contract fields stdout_sha256 and stderr_sha256 do not bind the command's actual output bytes. text=True with errors="replace" lossily normalizes output before hashing; distinct byte streams therefore produce the same recorded digest.
findings.reproduce:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=ops/devlane/harness/receipt python3 - <<'PY'
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import canonical,receipts
d=[]
for n in (255,254):
 _,out,_,_=receipts.run([sys.executable,'-c',f'import os; os.write(1,bytes([{n}]))'],Path.cwd())
 d.append(canonical.sha256_hex(out.encode('utf-8','replace')))
print(d); assert d[0]==d[1]
PY

findings.claim: The contract says tree_dirty records the state used and an admissible receipt requires false, but dirty_paths ignores git status's exit code. If Git cannot inspect the index, empty stdout is treated as a clean tree and an admissible-looking receipt is issued.
findings.reproduce: bash -eu -c 'r=$PWD; d=$(mktemp -d); git init -q "$d/repo"; printf x > "$d/repo/a"; git -C "$d/repo" add a; git -C "$d/repo" -c user.name=a -c user.email=a@b commit -qm one; printf corrupt > "$d/repo/.git/index"; (cd "$d/repo" && WF_AGENT="Audit <a@b>" python3 "$r/ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py" record --claim probe -- true); f=$(find "$d/repo/.dev/records/receipts" -name "*.json" -print -quit); grep -q '"tree_dirty":false' "$f"'

findings.claim: Checklist item 5 requires one sanitized refusal line. A missing command copies raw argv into Refusal.actual, and the adapter prints it without clean(); an argv newline injects a forged wire line and any credential argument is echoed into stderr/logs.
findings.reproduce:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - <<'PY'
import os,subprocess
arg='--token=FAKE-SECRET-DO-NOT-USE\nforged: expected pass; found pass; needed none'
env=dict(os.environ,WF_AGENT='Audit <a@b>')
p=subprocess.run(['python3','ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py','record','--claim','probe','--','definitely-no-such-command',arg],env=env,capture_output=True,text=True)
print(p.stderr); assert p.returncode==2 and len(p.stderr.splitlines())==2 and 'FAKE-SECRET-DO-NOT-USE' in p.stderr
PY

findings.claim: Checklist item 5 requires every refusal to use the single-line expected–found–needed wire. argparse exits before the try block for missing required arguments and emits two usage/error lines instead.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "import subprocess; p=subprocess.run(['python3','ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py','show'],capture_output=True,text=True); print(p.returncode,p.stderr); assert p.returncode==2 and not p.stdout and len(p.stderr.splitlines())==2 and not p.stderr.startswith('arguments: expected ')"

findings.claim: Checklist item 8 requires WF_AGENT in "Name <address>" form. The validation only looks for any '<' and a final '>', accepting empty or absent names and addresses and weakening receipt attribution.
findings.reproduce: WF_AGENT='<>' PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c "import runpy; n=runpy.run_path('ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py'); print(n['identity']()); assert n['identity']()=='<>'"

findings.claim: Observation: contract field argv is copied verbatim into receipts that checklist item 11 says are tracked. No rejection or credential-safe representation exists, so a command-line token is persisted into the repository record. No actual credential was found in this change.
findings.reproduce: bash -eu -c 'r=$PWD; d=$(mktemp -d); git init -q "$d"; printf x > "$d/a"; git -C "$d" add a; git -C "$d" -c user.name=a -c user.email=a@b commit -qm one; (cd "$d" && WF_AGENT="Audit <a@b>" python3 "$r/ops/devlane/harness/receipt.py" record --claim probe -- python3 -c pass --token FAKE-SECRET-DO-NOT-USE); rg -l "FAKE-SECRET-DO-NOT-USE" "$d/.dev/records/receipts"'

envelope.note: Read both inputs, all governing docs, the complete target implementation/modules/tests, records, and contract. Covered argv/shell, SQL/template, credentials, path/ref containment, sandbox claims, vendor-output checks, and supply-chain changes. No SQL/template seam, actual credential signature, sandbox-record mismatch, dependency/lockfile/action change, or shell=True execution was found; the four extracted module blob IDs match the checklist. Checklist decisions 6 and 12 were not treated as defects. The two committed receipts passed CUE vet. The frozen unittest command could not execute because this read-only audit sandbox has no writable temporary directory; all 18 cases stopped in setup. Read-only, memfd, and mocked probes were used instead. Filesystem-mutating reproductions and races could not be exercised here. The session store was not read.
